archetype.name: Lost Season (pitching collapse)
archetype.definition: A year in which Kansas City's 2025 run prevention fell from fourth in the league to 26th, dragging a .500 team to 69-93 and last in the AL Central. A Bobby Witt Jr. MVP-caliber season and a decent lineup couldn't hold it up.

report.headline: The pitching that carried 2025 gave way, and Witt couldn't cover it alone

recap.finish: 69-93, fifth in the AL Central and 16 games behind Cleveland; missed the postseason
recap.body:
This Royals team was built to prevent runs, and in 2026 it stopped preventing them. A year earlier the staff posted a 3.73 ERA, ranked fourth in runs allowed, and covered for an offense that ranked 26th. This year the offense was actually a little better, with a .718 OPS against .706 and a rank of 22nd instead of 26th. The pitching, though, swelled to a 4.77 ERA and ranked 26th in runs allowed. Over the season they gave up 810 runs and scored 690, a -120 margin, or -0.74 per game, 27th in the league. W vs Run Diff sits at -0.2, so the record is an honest reflection of the margin. This was not a decent team losing coin flips. It was a bad one.

The season was effectively lost by June. April went 10-17 and May 10-18, and in May the offense managed only 95 runs, leaving them 22-37. June and July were roughly break-even in record (13-14, 11-14) while still losing on runs. August was the one stretch where things worked: 16-11 with a +13 run margin. September then erased it, going 7-17 and getting outscored by 37. The last ten games went 2-8, including 12- and 14-run outbursts allowed to Cleveland and Chicago at home.

Bobby Witt Jr. was the season. He produced 7.0 WAR with a 119 wRC+, 45 steals and 17 Def Runs at shortstop, and he ranked first among 51 at his position. Carter Jensen gave them a real catcher bat: 27 home runs, a 116 wRC+ and 3.7 WAR. Jac Caglianone was the lineup's best hitter by rate at 129 wRC+. Those three were the C-graded lineup's reason to exist. The rest averaged out to roughly league-average production, apart from two heavy drags. Salvador Perez took 627 plate appearances as the DH with a .274 OBP, a 77 wRC+ and -1.1 WAR. Isaac Collins took 519 plate appearances at an 83 wRC+. The defense behind the pitchers was fine, at 20.6 Fielding Runs (seventh), so the run-prevention collapse sits on the mound.

The rotation earned its D+ and was flimsier than its top line suggests. Michael Wacha made the All-Star team and logged 200-plus innings at a 3.32 ERA, but his FIP was 4.38. Seth Lugo had the same 4.38 FIP and wore a 5.17 ERA. Noah Cameron was the most trustworthy arm by the peripherals, with a 3.92 FIP and 2.8 WAR. Behind those three, Luinder Avila walked 13.6% of batters before landing on the 60-day IL. The F bullpen was the worst unit on the team. Its five most-used relievers combined for -1.4 WAR. Saves were split among Lucas Erceg (13), Alex Lange (10) and Steven Cruz (8). Erceg and Lange both posted ERAs over 5.50 and walked 12% or more of hitters, so there was never a settled late inning.

After a 2024 playoff team and an 82-80 follow-up, this is the kind of drop that reframes the build. The position-player core is real and the defense holds. But the run-prevention identity of the last two years did not survive, and nothing in the record suggests bad luck took it away.

highlights.title: Witt carried an entire lineup
highlights.body: Witt's 7.0 WAR came from every direction: a 119 wRC+, 45 steals and 17 Def Runs at shortstop. That is roughly double the next-best Royal. He ranked first at his position on the site. The profile is broad enough that it doesn't depend on any one skill holding up.

highlights.title: Jensen and Caglianone gave real thump
highlights.body: Jensen hit 27 home runs with a 116 wRC+ while catching 149 games, worth 3.7 WAR. Caglianone's 129 wRC+ was the best rate bat on the roster, though his -5.9 Def Runs in the outfield gave some of it back. Together with Witt they are the reason the offense improved on 2025 even as the team got worse.

highlights.title: The defense held its standard
highlights.body: The defense finished seventh in Fielding Runs at 20.6. That is in line with the 19.5 and 22.5 of the previous two years, so it looks like a durable team trait rather than a fluke. It also isolates the blame for the runs allowed on the pitching staff.

lowlights.title: Run prevention fell off a cliff
lowlights.body: The staff went from fourth in runs allowed with a 3.73 ERA in 2025 to 26th with a 4.77 ERA, more than a run per nine worse. The fielders were just as good, so this is a pitching problem. It came from both the rotation (D+) and the bullpen (F), the identity the team had been built on.

lowlights.title: A bullpen with no answers
lowlights.body: Lange (6.75 ERA, -1.1 WAR) and Erceg (5.59 ERA) shared the closing job while walking 12% and 14% of batters. Cruz missed bats at 26.4% but carried a 5.16 FIP. Daniel Lynch IV, the most-used reliever, was merely serviceable. Walk rates like those are a skill problem, not bad luck, and the group needs rebuilding rather than waiting.

lowlights.title: Perez's DH line sank the lineup
lowlights.body: Perez took 627 plate appearances, second-most on the team. He posted a .274 OBP and a 77 wRC+, good for -1.1 WAR, ranking 29th of 36 at DH. He drove in 78 runs, but at a bat-only position that production level costs a lineup more than any other single spot. Collins' 83 wRC+ in 519 plate appearances compounded it.

arc.note: A 20-35 April-May buried the season. The summer drifted near .500 in record before August's 16-11 surge, the only month they outscored opponents. That was followed by a 7-17 September that ended with eight losses in the last ten.

recap.nextYear: The lineup has a real foundation. Witt, Jensen and Caglianone combined for 13.3 WAR, and the defense has saved roughly 20 runs three years running. The fastest offensive gain is simply replacing the DH and outfield production that Perez and Collins supplied. The pitching is where the work is. Wacha's 3.32 ERA ran more than a run ahead of his 4.38 FIP, so the All-Star season is unlikely to repeat as-is. Lugo's 5.17 ERA against the same FIP should bounce back some, which partly offsets it. Cameron is the steadiest starter by the peripherals. Beyond that trio the rotation thins quickly, and Avila ended the year on the 60-day IL. The bullpen graded F with walk problems throughout and needs new arms, not patience. Nothing here was luck: the -0.2 W vs Run Diff says this team earned its 69 wins. A return to 2024-25 levels means getting the run prevention back, not waiting for close games to break their way.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the record matches the run differential, and the two-year history clarifies the cause.
